name: Attack and defence
goal: You can see which pieces each side attacks, take a piece that is left undefended, and save an attacked piece by moving it, guarding it, blocking the attack or taking the attacker.

name: Getting out of check
goal: You can tell when a king is in check and find every way out: move the king, block the check, or take the checking piece.

name: Mate in one
goal: You can tell checkmate from check, and find a mate in one move when there is one.

name: What the pieces are worth
goal: You can count material with the usual values (pawn 1, knight and bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9), and tell a good trade from a bad one.

name: Opening principles
goal: In the first moves of any game, you can claim the centre with pawns, bring out knights and bishops, castle early, and avoid moving one piece again and again.

name: Mate with king and queen
goal: You can mate a lone king with king and queen, pushing it to the edge without giving stalemate.

name: Spot the threat
goal: After each of your opponent's moves, you can ask what it threatens, and find a move that deals with the threat.

name: Double attacks
goal: You can find a move that attacks two things at once, often with the queen, so the opponent cannot save both.

name: Forks
goal: You can spot a fork by a knight, a bishop or a pawn, see why a fork that gives check wins the other piece, and use a check to set one up.

name: Stopping the early queen attack
goal: As Black, you can stop Scholar's Mate and other early queen attacks, and gain time by developing while you attack the queen.

name: Mate with two rooks
goal: You can mate a lone king with two rooks, taking turns to push it rank by rank to the edge.

name: Pins
goal: You can pin a piece to a more valuable one behind it, and win the pinned piece by attacking it again.

name: Blunder check
goal: Before you play a move, you can look at what your opponent could take, check or attack after it, and pick a safer move when the answer is bad.

name: Italian Game
goal: As White, you can play the Italian Game: aim the bishop at f7, put pawns on c3 and d4 to build a centre, and castle.

name: Mate with king and rook
goal: You can mate a lone king with king and rook, using your king to help and a waiting move when you need one.

name: Back-rank mate
goal: You can mate a king trapped behind its own pawns on the back rank, and give your own king an escape square in time.

name: Skewers
goal: You can attack a valuable piece so that, when it moves away, you win the piece behind it.

name: Pawns: promotion and en passant
goal: You can promote a pawn, tell with the square of the pawn whether a king can catch it, and capture en passant.

name: Checks, captures and threats
goal: You can list every check, capture and threat for both sides before choosing a move, and find the forcing move that wins.

name: London System
goal: As White, you can set up the London System: the bishop out to f4 before the e-pawn moves to e3, pawns on d4, e3 and c3, and knights on f3 and d2.

name: Discovered attacks
goal: You can move one piece out of the way so that the piece behind it attacks, and use the moving piece to attack something else too.

name: Stalemate and other draws
goal: You can avoid stalemate when you are winning, aim for it when you are losing, and know the other draws: repetition and too few pieces left to mate.

name: Two Knights Defence
goal: As Black against the Italian Game, you can play the Two Knights Defence and know how to meet the attack on f7.

name: Removing the defender
goal: You can win a piece by taking or chasing away its only defender, or by giving that defender two jobs at once.

name: Discovered check and double check
goal: You can move one piece out of the way so the piece behind it gives check while the moved piece attacks something else. You can also use a double check, which the king can only answer by moving.

name: The king in the endgame
goal: Once the queens have been traded, you can bring your king into the game to attack pawns and support your own.

name: Queen's Gambit
goal: As White, you can offer the c-pawn with the Queen's Gambit, and win it back while you develop when Black takes it.

name: Active pieces and the centre
goal: When nothing can be won at once, you can improve a piece by putting it on a square where it controls more, especially in the centre.

name: Mate in two
goal: You can find a mate in two moves by first taking away the king's escape squares or forcing it where you want it.

name: Caro-Kann Defence
goal: As Black against 1.e4, you can play the Caro-Kann: support d5 with the c-pawn on c6, bring out the bishop on c8 early, and keep a solid position.

name: Queen's Gambit Declined
goal: As Black against the Queen's Gambit, you can hold the centre with the e-pawn on e6, develop, castle, and know which pieces still need to come out.

name: Candidate moves and thinking ahead
goal: You can list two or three candidate moves, look a few moves ahead in each, and choose with the opponent's best reply in mind.

name: King and pawn endgames
goal: You can tell whether king and pawn win against a lone king, using the opposition and the key squares in front of the pawn.

name: Using a pin
goal: You can attack a pinned piece with a pawn, add attackers to it, and take advantage of a pinned piece that can no longer defend.

name: Deflection
goal: You can force a defending piece away from the square or piece it guards, often with a sacrifice, and then win what it guarded.

name: Ruy Lopez
goal: As White, you can play the main line of the Ruy Lopez, and know why the bishop attacks the knight that guards e5.

name: Decoy
goal: You can lure a king or queen onto a square where a fork, a pin or a mate is waiting.

name: Zugzwang
goal: You can win a position where the opponent would be fine if they could pass, by making the move that leaves them only bad moves.

name: Simple plans
goal: You can make a small plan from the position: improve your worst piece, attack a weak pawn, or bring a rook to an open file.

name: Mating patterns
goal: You can recognise the smothered mate and other common mating patterns, and play the moves that lead to them.

name: Scotch Game
goal: As White, you can open the centre at once with the Scotch Game, and develop quickly when Black takes on d4.

name: Passed pawns
goal: You can make a passed pawn from a pawn majority, use an outside passed pawn to pull the enemy king away, and stop an enemy passed pawn.

name: Weak pawns
goal: You can recognise isolated, doubled and backward pawns, attack them in your opponent's position, and avoid them in yours.

name: In-between moves
goal: Before you recapture or answer a threat, you can look for a stronger move to play first, such as a check or a bigger threat.

name: Opening traps
goal: You can spot common opening traps, such as attacks on f2 and f7, and avoid falling into them.

name: Trapping a piece
goal: You can win a piece that has no safe square left, and keep your own pieces from walking into a trap.

name: Breakthroughs and pawn races
goal: You can break through a pawn wall with a pawn sacrifice, and count who promotes first in a race.

name: Pawn chains and breaks
goal: You can read a pawn chain, attack it at its base with a pawn break, and tell open positions from closed ones.

name: Clearing and blocking lines
goal: You can move a piece off a square or line so another piece can use it, and put a piece between an enemy piece and what it defends.

name: Sicilian Defence
goal: As Black against 1.e4, you can play the Sicilian Defence: trade your c-pawn for White's d-pawn, then build the Dragon set-up with ...g6, ...Bg7, castling and ...Nc6.

name: Rook endgame basics
goal: You can keep your rook active, put it behind a passed pawn, and cut the enemy king off from the pawn.

name: Weak squares and outposts
goal: You can find a square that no enemy pawn can attack, and put a knight or another piece there.

name: Quiet moves
goal: You can find a winning move that is not a check or a capture, such as one that cuts off the king or makes a threat that cannot be met.

name: French Defence
goal: As Black against 1.e4, you can play the French Defence and know the plan against White's pawn chain: attack its base with ...c5 and its front with ...f6.

name: Rook endgames: Lucena and Philidor
goal: You can win the Lucena position by building a bridge, and draw the Philidor position with the defending rook on the third rank.

name: Open files and the seventh rank
goal: You can put a rook on an open file, put your second rook on the same file, and use a rook on the seventh rank to attack pawns and trap the king.

name: Perpetual check
goal: When you are losing, you can see when checks that never stop will save the game with a draw.

name: Gambits
goal: You can judge when a pawn offered in the opening is worth taking, and when to give one back to finish developing.

name: Good and bad pieces
goal: You can tell a good bishop from a bad one blocked by its own pawns, use the two bishops, and decide when a knight is better than a bishop.

name: Bishop and knight endgames
goal: You can tell when a bishop beats a knight and when the reverse is true, and know two draws: bishops of opposite colours, and the wrong bishop with a rook pawn.

name: Combining Themes
goal: You can see when one forcing move, such as a decoy or a clearing sacrifice, sets up a second Theme that wins.

name: When to trade pieces
goal: Before a trade, you can look at king safety, material and the pieces it would remove, and decide whether to trade or to keep the pieces on.

name: Attacking the king
goal: You can attack a king with more pieces than defend it, open lines towards it, and punish a king left in the centre.

name: Defending
goal: When your king is under attack, you can name the threat and stop it, look for a forcing move of your own, trade off the strongest attacker, or give back material to break the attack.
